summary: Prod dedicated pool throughput regression caused by ephemeral customer sidecar cohort creating GPU slot fragmentation and autoscaler misclassification
estimated_impact: Throughput on BrightHome AI reserved pool dropped ~35% for a 90-minute window; p99 request latency rose from 420ms to 1.3s; single-customer tail event but caused autoscaler responses impacting adjacent tenants.
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightHome AI observed degraded throughput and elevated p99 latency for their dedicated pool during daytime peak. Symptoms included sudden slot fragmentation (many small GPU attachments that never consolidated), autoscaler repeatedly scaling down after short-lived attach spikes, and brief regional GPU shortages that triggered cross-tenant fallback routing. Impact was limited to the BrightHome reserved cluster but autoscaler oscillation caused transient performance variance for other dedicated tenants in the stripe.

Impact:
- BrightHome AI production routes experienced ~35% throughput reduction and increased failures on batched routes.
- Autoscaler made multiple downscaling decisions that later had to be reversed, causing thrash and occasional 5xx fallbacks for low-priority routes.

Timeline (local times, PDT):
- 07:50 — Support received first alert from BrightHome (console p99 spike).
- 07:58 — Automated alert triggered: reserved-pool-attach-lag-high (us-west-2).
- 08:05 — Support triaged and engaged SRE on-call.
- 08:12 — SRE noted many small ephemeral attachments and high connection churn from BrightHome sidecar hosts.
- 08:30 — Mitigation applied: temporary per-tenant throttle on sidecar connection concurrency; model pin for BrightHome to redwood-open-7b-v2 to reduce model migration.
- 09:10 — Autoscaler damping parameter adjusted for the affected stripe to avoid aggressive downscale.
- 10:20 — Stability confirmed; p99 and throughput returned to baseline.

Wanted: full root-cause analysis, permanent mitigation, and runbook updates to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sidecar creates many short-lived connections and dispatches small single-request streams to reserved pool (high fanout).
2) Serving runtime allocates many fractional GPU slots to satisfy quick attaches (fragmentation).
3) Autoscaler observes short high-attach spike then rapid drop and executes downscale decisions due to current hysteresis settings.
4) Downscale removes capacity; when more real traffic arrives, allocator can't consolidate fragmented slots quickly leading to p99 spike and fallbacks.

comments: BrightHome (customer): We're seeing a lot of 502s and p99 latency spikes starting ~08:00 PDT. Aisha opened the ticket referencing our reserved pool.
Support (Aisha): Investigating; I've escalated to SRE and asked for allocator dumps and autoscaler logs.

SRE (Tom): Noted high connection churn from a small cohort of sidecar hosts; appears to be many short streams (single token-ish requests) interleaving. Starting temporary throttle on their connection concurrency.
Support: Customer accepted throttle test; reported immediate reduction in failures within 15 minutes.
SRE (Tom): Adjusted autoscaler downscale hysteresis to 6m for the stripe. Monitoring for oscillation.
investigation_notes: Collected allocator snapshots, prefetched KV cache usage, and sidecar host connection histograms for tenant=brighthome.
Found that 12 sidecar hosts (cohort) were generating >200 short-lived attaches/min with payloads of ~100 tokens, causing many fractional slot allocations (avg slot occupancy 0.12 GPU).
KV cache grew for the tenant due to many distinct short contexts, preventing efficient reuse and hurting consolidation heuristics.
Autoscaler logs showed repeated downscale decisions triggered 2–3 minutes after transient attach drops; current hysteresis at 90s was too short for this workload pattern.
No kernel-level GPU faults or driver errors observed; GPU contention was logical (fragmentation) rather than thermal or hardware failure.
Cross-checked with console traces; adjacent tenants saw minor p99 blips correlated with autoscaler down/up cycles.
root_cause: A cohort of BrightHome AI sidecar hosts created high-frequency, short-lived connection streams that led to fractional GPU slot allocation (slot fragmentation). The autoscaler misinterpreted the short spike as a sustained drop shortly thereafter (hysteresis too short) and downscaled, which removed capacity that could have been used to absorb subsequent real traffic. Net effect: temporary GPU shortages and throughput regression in the dedicated pool.
resolution:
1) Applied temporary throttle on BrightHome sidecar concurrency and recommended batching changes on their side (customer implemented).
2) Increased autoscaler downscale hysteresis for the affected stripe to 6 minutes to avoid reacting to short spikes.
3) Deployed allocator change to prefer consolidation of fractional attachments when tenant KV cache indicates repeated small contexts.
4) Restored normal capacity after monitoring showed stabilization.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering: Merge PR to add heuristic in allocator that delays slot fragmentation for short-lived attaches (PR linked).
2) Infra: Add autoscaler metric smoothing to avoid downscaling on sub-5m fluctuations for dedicated stripes (ticket opened).
3) Support: Update runbook with 'ephemeral sidecar cohort' checklist and troubleshooting query templates.
4) Customer: BrightHome to roll out sidecar batching changes and limit keepalive churn; agreed to a partnership call to tune client SDK.
5) Monitoring: Add a dashboard panel showing fractional-slot occupancy per tenant and an alert when >25% fragmentation persists >10m.
monitoring: New alerts created: reserved.pool.fragmentation.high (threshold 25% for 10m), autoscaler.downscale-spike (freq >2 in 10m).
Post-fix: p99 latency returned to baseline within 70 minutes of mitigation; no further downscale thrash observed.
customer_communication: Customer notified 2026-03-12 10:30 PDT with root-cause summary and recommended client SDK changes. BrightHome confirmed they will throttle their sidecar and implement batching in next release. Support to run weekly checks for two weeks.
